content: 1. Ansetron and solifenacin both prolong the QTc interval. These drugs should be avoided or alternative medications should be considered. They are contraindicated in patients with congenital long QT syndrome. ECG monitoring is recommended when used with other QT-prolonging drugs, electrolyte abnormalities, congestive heart failure (CHF), or bradyarrhythmias. 2. Ondansetron and sotalol both increase the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. These drugs should not be used in patients with congenital long QT syndrome. ECG monitoring is advised when combined with other QT-prolonging agents, electrolyte imbalances, CHF, or bradyarrhythmias. 3. Sotorasib reduces the levels or effects of ondansetron via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, refer to the prescribing information of the P-gp substrate for dosage adjustments. 4. Ondansetron and sumatriptan increase each other's toxicity by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 5. Ondansetron and sumatriptan intranasal increase each other's toxicity by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 6. Ondansetron and sunitinib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. These drugs should not be used in patients with congenital long QT syndrome. ECG monitoring is recommended when combined with other QT-prolonging agents, electrolyte abnormalities, CHF, or bradyarrhythmias. 7. Ondansetron and tacrolimus both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. These drugs should not be used in patients with congenital long QT syndrome. ECG monitoring is recommended when combined with other QT-prolonging agents, electrolyte abnormalities, CHF, or bradyarrhythmias. 8. Tedizolid and ondansetron enhance each other's effects through pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Both drugs increase serotonin levels, raising the risk of serotonin syndrome. 9. Ondansetron and telavancin both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. These drugs should not be used in patients with congenital long QT syndrome. ECG monitoring is recommended when combined with other QT-prolonging agents, electrolyte abnormalities, CHF, or bradyarrhythmias. 10. Tepotinib increases the levels or effects of ondansetron via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If concomitant use is unavoidable, reduce the P-gp substrate dosage as recommended in its product labeling. 11. Tetrabenazine and ondansetron both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 12. Thioridazine and ondansetron both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. These drugs should not be used in patients with congenital long QT syndrome. ECG monitoring is recommended when combined with other QT-prolonging agents, electrolyte abnormalities, CHF, or bradyarrhythmias. 13. Ondansetron and thiothixene both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. These drugs should not be used in patients with congenital long QT syndrome. ECG monitoring is recommended when combined with other QT-prolonging agents, electrolyte abnormalities, CHF, or bradyarrhythmias. 14. Ondansetron and toremifene both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. These drugs should not be used in patients with congenital long QT syndrome. ECG monitoring is recommended when combined with other QT-prolonging agents, electrolyte abnormalities, CHF, or bradyarrhythmias. 15. Ondansetron and tranylcypromine increase each other's toxicity by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 16. Ondansetron and trimipramine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 17. Ondansetron and trimipramine increase each other's toxicity by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 18. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of ondansetron by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Avoid concomitant use of tucatinib with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious or life-threatening toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose according to product labeling. 19. Ondansetron increases the toxicity of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Exercise extreme caution when vilanterol is co-administered with drugs that prolong the QTc interval, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 20. Vandetanib and ondansetron both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. These drugs should not be used in patients with congenital long QT syndrome. ECG monitoring is recommended when combined with other QT-prolonging agents, electrolyte abnormalities, CHF, or bradyarrhythmias. 21. Ondansetron and vardenafil both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. These drugs should not be used in patients with congenital long QT syndrome. ECG monitoring is recommended when combined with other QT-prolonging agents, electrolyte abnormalities, CHF, or bradyarrhythmias. 22. Ondansetron and vemurafenib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. These drugs should not be used in patients with congenital long QT syndrome. ECG monitoring is recommended when combined with other QT-prolonging agents, electrolyte abnormalities, CHF, or bradyarrhythmias. 23. Ondansetron and venlafaxine increase each other's toxicity by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 24. Ondansetron increases the toxicity of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. Exercise extreme caution when vilanterol is co-administered with drugs that prolong the QTc interval, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 25. Ondansetron and voriconazole both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. These drugs should not be used in patients with congenital long QT syndrome. ECG monitoring is recommended when combined with other QT-prolonging agents, electrolyte abnormalities, CHF, or bradyarrhythmias. 26. Voriconazole increases the levels or effects of ondansetron by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 27. Ondansetron and vorinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. These drugs should not be used in patients with congenital long QT syndrome. ECG monitoring is recommended when combined with other QT-prolonging agents, electrolyte abnormalities, CHF, or bradyarrhythmias. 28. Ziprasidone and ondansetron both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. These drugs should not be used in patients with congenital long QT syndrome. ECG monitoring is recommended when combined with other QT-prolonging agents, electrolyte abnormalities, CHF, or bradyarrhythmias. 29. Ondansetron and zolmitriptan increase each other's toxicity by elevating serotonin levels. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 30. Albuterol and ondansetron both prolong the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 31. Ondansetron and alfuzosin both prolong the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 32. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of ondansetron by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor closely. No dosage adjustment for ondansetron is recommended for patients on these drugs. 33. Atazanavir increases the levels or effects of ondansetron by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor closely. CYP450 inhibitors may decrease the clearance of ondansetron. However, no dosage adjustment for ondansetron is recommended. 34. Ondansetron and bedaquiline both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. ECG should be monitored closely. 35. Berotralstat increases the levels or effects of ondansetron via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use with caution and monitor closely. Monitor or titrate the P-gp substrate dose if co-administered. 36. Bosutinib increases the levels of ondansetron via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use with caution and monitor closely. 37. Butabarbital decreases the levels or effects of ondansetron by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor closely. No dosage adjustment for ondansetron is recommended for patients on these drugs. 38. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of ondansetron by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. It also decreases ondansetron levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor closely. 39. Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of ondansetron by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Increase the dose of the CYP3A4 substrate as needed when co-administered with cenobamate. 40. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of ondansetron by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 41. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ondansetron by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor closely. 42. Crizotinib increases the levels of ondansetron via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use with caution and monitor closely. 43. Crofelemer increases the levels of ondansetron by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor closely. Crofelemer has the potential to inhibit CYP3A4 at concentrations expected in the gut but is unlikely to inhibit it systemically due to minimal absorption. 44. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of ondansetron by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 45. Danicopan increases the levels or effects of ondansetron via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use with caution and monitor closely. Danicopan increases plasma concentrations of P-gp substrates; consider dose reduction of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious adverse reactions. 46. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of ondansetron by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor closely. CYP450 inhibitors may decrease the clearance of ondansetron. However, no dosage adjustment for ondansetron is recommended. 47. Deferasirox decreases the levels or effects of ondansetron by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor closely. 48. Deutetrabenazine and ondansetron both prolong the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically relevant extent. Certain circumstances may increase the risk of torsades de pointes and/or sudden death in association with drugs that prolong the QTc interval (e.g., bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, co-administration with other QTc-prolonging drugs, presence of congenital QT prolongation). 49. Dexamethasone decreases the levels or effects of ondansetron by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor closely. No dosage adjustment for ondansetron is recommended for patients on these drugs. 50. Dichlorphenamide and ondansetron both decrease serum potassium. Use with caution and monitor closely. 51. Doxepin and ondansetron both prolong the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 52. Efavirenz decreases the levels or effects of ondansetron by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor closely. 53. Elagolix increases the levels or effects of ondansetron via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Elagolix decreases ondansetron levels by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates if co-administered. Consider increasing the CYP3A substrate dose if needed. 54. Eliglustat increases the levels of ondansetron via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor therapeutic drug concentrations as indicated, or consider reducing the dosage of the P-gp substrate and titrate to clinical effect. 55. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases the levels of ondansetron by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Cobicistat is a CYP3A4 inhibitor; contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates for which elevated plasma concentrations are associated with serious and/or life-threatening events. 56. Encorafenib affects hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor closely. Encorafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Co-administration of encorafenib with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may result in increased toxicity or decreased efficacy of these agents. 57. Fedratinib increases the levels or effects of ondansetron by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor closely. Adjust the dose of drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. 58. Ondansetron decreases the effects of fenfluramine by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use with caution and monitor closely. Potent serotonin receptor antagonists may decrease fenfluramine efficacy. If co-administered, monitor appropriately. 59. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of ondansetron by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor closely. CYP450 inhibitors may decrease the clearance of ondansetron. However, no dosage adjustment for ondansetron is recommended. 60. Ondansetron and fostemsavir both prolong the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 61. Gadobenate and ondansetron both prolong the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 62. Ondansetron and gemtuzumab both prolong the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. 63. Gepirone and ondansetron both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 64. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases the levels or effects of ondansetron via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use with caution and monitor closely. 65. Goserelin increases the toxicity of ondansetron by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. This combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 66. Histrelin increases the toxicity of ondansetron by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. This combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 67. Hydroxyzine increases the toxicity of ondansetron by prolonging the QTc interval. Use with caution and monitor closely. This combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 68. Iloperidone increases the levels of ondansetron by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor closely. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may lead to increased plasma levels of drugs predominantly eliminated by CYP3A4. 69. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of ondansetron by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor closely. CYP450 inhibitors may decrease the clearance of ondansetron. However, no dosage adjustment for ondansetron is recommended. 70. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of ondansetron by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor closely. CYP450 inhibitors may decrease the clearance of ondansetron. However, no dosage adjustment for ondansetron is recommended. 71. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of ondansetron by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use with caution and monitor closely. Istradefylline 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials. This effect was not observed with istradefylline 20 mg/day. Istradefylline also increases the levels or effects of ondansetron via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use with caution and monitor closely. Istradefylline 40 mg/day increased peak levels and AUC of P-gp substrates in clinical trials. Consider dose reduction of sensitive P-gp substrates.
